stories.title: Evolutionary game study on green finance promoting low-carbon production in manufacturing enterprises under the industrial internet platform
stories.description: Industrial Internet platforms are emerging as a key driver of digital transformation and low-carbon transition in manufacturing by integrating next-generation digital technologies with industrial production. At the same time, green finance has become an important policy instrument for supporting industrial decarbonization. However, how digital empowerment and green finance jointly shape manufacturing enterprises’ low-carbon production decisions remains insufficiently understood. Here, we develop a three-party evolutionary game model involving industrial Internet platforms, platform-affiliated manufacturing enterprises, and banks based on digital empowerment theory, sustainable development theory, and evolutionary game theory. Dynamic simulations are conducted to investigate the strategic interactions and evolutionary dynamics among these stakeholders under different scenarios. We find that the initial strategic choices of all participants influence the evolutionary trajectories and equilibrium outcomes of the system. For industrial Internet platforms, the cost of providing digital empowerment services, the digital empowerment cost coefficient, and the basic empowerment cost substantially shape manufacturing enterprises’ willingness to adopt low-carbon production. On the financial side, banks’ net returns from green credit, green lending interest rates, and the additional revenue generated through green credit further strengthen enterprises’ incentives to pursue low-carbon production strategies. These results demonstrate that effective digital empowerment and well-designed green financial incentives reinforce one another in facilitating the low-carbon transformation of manufacturing enterprises. Our findings highlight the importance of accelerating the development and diffusion of industrial Internet platforms while improving the design of green financial mechanisms to promote sustainable manufacturing. The study also provides new insights into the micro-level interaction mechanisms among digital platforms, manufacturing enterprises, and financial institutions, offering theoretical support and practical guidance for optimizing green finance policies and advancing high-quality, low-carbon industrial development.

stories.title: Ultraviolet-A light-induced chronic hyperploidization causes fibrosis in post-mitotic cells affected by Fuchs endothelial corneal dystrophy
stories.description: Fuchs endothelial corneal dystrophy (FECD) is a progressive disorder characterized by corneal endothelial (CE) cell loss and accumulation of extracellular matrix (ECM) excrescences (guttae) in Descemet’s membrane, leading to corneal edema and visual impairment. We previously demonstrated that ultraviolet-A (UVA) exposure induces oxidative stress and CE cell loss in a non-genetic murine model of FECD. Here, we investigated whether UVA triggers polyploidization, a conserved stress-adaptation mechanism observed in several post-mitotic tissues. Using our UVA-based FECD model, we performed temporal analyses of CE cell ploidy, and molecular markers associated with cell-cycle regulation and ECM deposition seen in FECD. UVA exposure induced oxidative DNA damage and apoptosis, resulting in decreased cell density. Surviving CE cells re-entered the cell cycle and underwent endocycling, generating enlarged polyploid nuclei in about 60% of cells with increased DNA content reaching up to 64 C by day 3, compared to 6 C at day 1 post-UVA. Early polyploidization served a compensatory role preserving tissue integrity following cell loss. However, persistent oxidative stress promoted progression toward endomitosis and multinucleation, accompanied by cellular senescence and fibrosis observed during disease progression. Mechanistically, UVA-induced cell-cycle re-entry and polyploidization were mediated by YAP1 and its downstream effectors, E2F1 and CDK2. Pharmacologic inhibition of YAP1 using the small-molecule CA3 suppressed polyploidization-associated multinucleation and reduced pro-fibrotic changes, ultimately mitigating CE cell loss in vivo. Together, these findings identify distinct early protective and later pathogenic roles of polyploidization in CE cells and highlight YAP1-mediated hyperploidization as a potential therapeutic target for FECD.

stories.title: First genomic report of epidemic super-lineage, clade 2.5.6 Acinetobacter baumannii from hospital environmental surfaces in Bangladesh
stories.description: The World Health Organization classifies Acinetobacter baumannii as a critical-priority carbapenem-resistant nosocomial pathogen. Hospitals are underrecognized reservoirs of multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria, yet Bangladesh has limited environmental genomic surveillance, especially of International Clone 2 (IC2). A. baumannii was isolated and genomically characterized from 95 environment samples collected at two district-level hospitals in Jashore, Bangladesh. Biochemical characterization identified 38 isolates as Acinetobacter spp. (40%), of which 86% were moderate-to-strong biofilm formers and universally carbapenem-resistant. International Clone 2 (IC2) was identified by multiplex PCR using three isolates. Whole-genome sequencing was performed on two representative isolates, 2GbA2_JUST (pneumonia ward bed, XDR) and A_38_JUST (toilet dam water, MDR) and MLST analysis grouped them as ST2. Capybara SNP barcode categorization positively identified both samples as Epidemic Super-Lineage Clade 2.5.6. Resistome profiling found 28 ARGs per isolate, including OXA-66, plasmid-borne OXA-23, armA, ADC-73, and three full RND efflux systems. Virulome analysis found 17 functional virulence categories. Analysis of 37 A. baumannii genomes revealed an open pangenome (γ = 0.301). To our knowledge, this study provides the first genomic characterization of Epidemic Super Lineage (ESL) Clade 2.5.6 Acinetobacter baumannii recovered from hospital environmental surfaces in Bangladesh.
